results.title: Data Preprocessing in Machine Learning - Jyotiprakash's Blog
results.content: # Data Preprocessing in Machine Learning #data-preprocessing Data preprocessing is the essential art of refining raw, unpolished data into a clean, structured format that machine learning models can effectively utilize. Feature engineering follows, breathing new life into the data by crafting variables like age groups derived from birthdates. Real-time preprocessing transforms data on-the-fly—scaling a new transaction as it arrives—demanding lightweight, pre-fitted transformers (e.g., a saved scaler). Fitted on an 80/20 split, it predicts wine quality, with a report showing balanced performance—libraries like Pandas (data loading) and Scikit-learn (pipeline, scaling) shine here. We start by loading the data, handling missing values (e.g., imputing lot frontage with medians, flagging missing basements), and encoding categoricals (one-hot for nominal like zoning, ordinal for quality ratings). A pipeline ensures scaling and encoding fit only training data, avoiding leakage as new customers stream in. Preprocessing is the unsung hero of machine learning, transforming messy data into a foundation for insight.
